default.$description:
Intent:      The main page canvas — the base surface everything sits on
Use when:    Page background, main content area, any full-page layout surface
Do not use:  Cards, panels, modals, or elevated containers — use color/surface/* instead
Use instead: color/surface/default for cards and flat content containers
Foreground:  color/background/default/foreground
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Primary text and icon color on the default page background
Use when:    Headings, body text, labels, any text sitting directly on the page canvas
Do not use:  Text inside cards, modals, or colored containers — use that container's /foreground
Use instead: color/text/secondary for subdued text, color/text/disabled for inactive text
Status:      active

subtle.$description:
Intent:      A near-white tint for low-emphasis background sections
Use when:    Alternating section backgrounds, sidebar backgrounds, hover states on rows
Do not use:  Cards or elevated UI — subtle is a flat tint, not a raised surface
Use instead: color/surface/raised for slightly elevated containers
Note:        No /foreground pair — text on subtle uses color/background/default/foreground
Status:      active

muted.$description:
Intent:      A visible muted surface for de-emphasized sections or inactive areas
Use when:    Disabled input backgrounds, skeleton loaders, code blocks, tag backgrounds
Do not use:  Primary content areas or interactive surfaces
Use instead: color/background/default for the main page, color/background/subtle for softer tints
Foreground:  color/background/muted/foreground
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon color on muted background surfaces
Use when:    Placeholder text, captions inside muted containers, secondary labels on muted bg
Do not use:  Primary body text on the page canvas — contrast is intentionally reduced
Use instead: color/background/default/foreground for full-strength text
Status:      active
Note: 2026-09-22 → zinc/600 (slate) — zinc/500 was 4.34:1 on the muted fill after the slate swap.

inverted.$description:
Intent:      A dark surface for high-contrast inverted sections
Use when:    Dark hero sections, inverted banners, dark tooltips, dark notification bars
Do not use:  A whole page theme — this is a single inverted section within the page
Use instead: color/surface/overlay for floating dark elements like dropdowns
Foreground:  color/background/inverted/foreground
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon color on the inverted dark background
Use when:    All text and icons placed on color/background/inverted
Do not use:  On any light surface — white on white is invisible
Use instead: color/background/default/foreground on light surfaces
Status:      active

accent.$description:
Intent: Subtle background for hover states on ghost and text-style interactive elements.
Use when: Ghost button hover, sidebar item hover, command menu row hover, dropdown item hover. Maps to shadcn --accent.
Do not use: As a primary action fill — this is a hover tint, not a CTA color.
Use instead: color/brand/primary for primary action fills.
Foreground: color/brand/accent/foreground
Status: Stable

foreground.$description:
Intent: Text and icon color on top of color/brand/accent fill.
Use when: Labels and icons inside ghost button hover states, hovered sidebar items, hovered menu rows. Maps to shadcn --accent-foreground.
Do not use: On any surface other than color/brand/accent.
Use instead: color/background/default/foreground for text on default backgrounds.
Status: Stable

app.$description:
Intent:      The app background behind the floating panels — the tinted canvas the sidebar, page and chat panels sit on
Use when:    The outermost app shell area, the gaps between panels; later the base for a glass effect
Do not use:  Inside a panel (page content, cards) — use color/background/default or color/surface/*
Use instead: color/background/default for the page panel itself
Note:        Brand/50. Panels on top stay white.
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon directly on the app background
Use when:    Rare — text placed in the shell gaps (e.g. a loading message before panels mount)
Do not use:  Text inside panels
Use instead: color/background/default/foreground inside the page panel
Status:      active

app-glow.$description:
Intent:      Soft brand glow painted on color/background/app for subtle depth
Use when:    Radial gradients on the app shell background only
Do not use:  Fills, text, borders or any component
Use instead: color/background/app for the flat app background
Note:        Brand/300. Glows sit at the right, behind the page panel — never behind sidebar text.
Status:      active

secondary.$description:
Intent:      Subdued text for supporting information
Use when:    Captions, metadata, timestamps, helper text, secondary labels beneath a heading
Do not use:  Body text or headings — contrast is intentionally reduced for supporting roles
Use instead: color/background/default/foreground for primary body text and headings
Status:      active

disabled.$description:
Intent:      Text color for inactive or unavailable elements
Use when:    Disabled input labels, disabled button text, unavailable menu items
Do not use:  Any text that is interactive or readable — fails WCAG contrast at small sizes
Use instead: color/text/secondary for readable but de-emphasized text
Status:      active

inverse.$description:
Intent:      Text on dark surfaces where the default dark text would be invisible
Use when:    Text on color/background/inverted, dark banners, dark tooltips
Do not use:  Text on any light or white surface
Use instead: color/background/default/foreground on light surfaces
Status:      active

link.$description:
Intent:      Inline text link color on light surfaces
Use when:    Hyperlinks in body copy, navigation links, breadcrumbs
Do not use:  Buttons — links are inline text, buttons are interactive containers
Use instead: color/brand/primary for button fills, color/text/link-hover for the hovered state
Status:      active

link-hover.$description:
Intent:      Inline text link color on hover
Use when:    The :hover state of color/text/link — always used as a pair, never standalone
Do not use:  Default/resting link state — contrast is slightly higher than needed at rest
Use instead: color/text/link for the resting state
Status:      active

link-active.$description:
Intent:      Inline text link color on hover
Use when:    The :hover state of color/text/link — always used as a pair, never standalone
Do not use:  Default/resting link state — contrast is slightly higher than needed at rest
Use instead: color/text/link for the resting state
Status:      active

invalid.$description: Error/invalid text on default backgrounds. Use for form field labels, descriptions, and alert text in invalid or destructive states. NOT the same as status/danger-subtle/foreground (which requires a danger-subtle background).

default.$description:
Intent:      Standard border for input fields, radio buttons, and component frames
Use when:    Input borders at rest, checkbox outlines, card borders, component frame dividers
Do not use:  Focus states, hover states, or error states — use the dedicated state tokens
Use instead: color/border/hover on hover, color/border/focus on focus, color/border/error on error
Status:      active

subtle.$description:
Intent:      Low-contrast border for structural, non-interactive elements
Use when:    Internal card dividers, hairline row separators, layout structure on white bg
Do not use:  Input fields, interactive components, or any element requiring clear boundary definition
Use instead: color/border/default for input and component borders
Status:      active

strong.$description:
Intent:      High-emphasis border for selected or active states
Use when:    Selected option chips, active tabs, emphasized separators, drag handles
Do not use:  Default resting borders or focus rings
Use instead: color/border/default for standard borders, color/border/focus for focus
Status:      active

focus.$description:
Intent:      High-contrast focus ring for keyboard navigation and accessibility
Use when:    :focus-visible on buttons, inputs, links, and any interactive element
Do not use:  Decorative borders, hover states, or error indication
Use instead: color/border/error for validation errors, color/border/strong for emphasis
Status:      active

hover.$description:
Intent:      Slightly more prominent border when a user hovers an interactive element
Use when:    Input border on :hover, selectable card on :hover, interactive list item on :hover
Do not use:  Resting state or focus state
Use instead: color/border/default for resting state, color/border/focus for keyboard focus
Status:      active

disabled.$description:
Intent:      Low-contrast border indicating an interaction is unavailable
Use when:    Disabled input fields, disabled checkboxes, disabled select elements
Do not use:  Any interactive or enabled element
Use instead: color/border/default for the enabled equivalent
Status:      active

error.$description:
Intent:      Strong border to highlight form validation errors
Use when:    Input border in invalid/error state, failed form fields, required field alerts
Do not use:  Warning states — error signals failure, warning signals caution
Use instead: color/border/warning for cautionary non-failure states
Status:      active

success.$description:
Intent:      Border indicating a successful or valid state
Use when:    Input border after successful validation, confirmed selection borders
Do not use:  Neutral or warning states
Use instead: color/border/error for failed validation, color/border/warning for caution
Status:      active
Note: 2026-09-22 → green/600 (was green/700 — too dark as a badge outline).

warning.$description:
Intent:      Border indicating a cautionary or attention-required state
Use when:    Input border with a non-critical warning, fields approaching a limit
Do not use:  Actual errors or failed validation — warning is not failure
Use instead: color/border/error for validation failures
Status:      active

primary.$description:
Intent:      The main brand fill color for primary interactive elements
Use when:    Primary button fill, active toggle fill, selected chip fill, key CTAs
Do not use:  Text color on light backgrounds — use color/text/link for inline brand-colored text
Use instead: color/text/link for inline links, color/brand/secondary for lower-emphasis brand surfaces
Foreground:  color/brand/primary/foreground
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon color placed directly on a color/brand/primary fill
Use when:    Label inside a primary button, icon inside a filled brand badge
Do not use:  On any surface other than color/brand/primary — white on white is invisible
Use instead: color/background/default/foreground for text on neutral surfaces
Status:      active

primary-hover.$description:
Intent:      Darker brand fill for the hover state of a primary element
Use when:    Primary button :hover fill — always paired with color/brand/primary, never used standalone
Do not use:  Resting state or active/pressed state
Use instead: color/brand/primary for resting, color/brand/primary-active for pressed
Status:      active

primary-active.$description:
Intent:      Darkest brand fill for the pressed/active state of a primary element
Use when:    Primary button :active fill — the moment of click or tap
Do not use:  Hover or resting states
Use instead: color/brand/primary-hover for hover, color/brand/primary for resting
Status:      active

secondary.$description:
Intent:      Light brand-tinted surface for lower-emphasis brand presence
Use when:    Secondary button fill, selected row highlight, brand-tinted badge background, active nav item background
Do not use:  High-emphasis CTAs — too light to read as a primary action
Use instead: color/brand/primary for high-emphasis filled actions
Foreground:  color/brand/secondary/foreground
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon color on a color/brand/secondary fill
Use when:    Label inside a secondary brand button, text inside a brand-tinted badge
Do not use:  On white or neutral surfaces — too dark-blue for general body text
Use instead: color/text/link for inline brand-colored text on neutral backgrounds
Status:      active

destructive.$description:
Intent: Fill color for destructive CTA elements — buttons that delete, remove, or permanently alter data.
Use when: Delete buttons, Remove confirmations, destructive dialog primary actions. Maps to shadcn --destructive.
Do not use: For status indicators, error messages, or form validation — use color/status/danger for those.
Use instead: color/status/danger for inline error states and validation feedback.
Foreground: color/brand/destructive/foreground
Status: Stable

foreground.$description:
Intent: Text and icon color on top of color/brand/destructive fill.
Use when: Labels and icons inside destructive buttons and confirmation CTAs. Maps to shadcn --destructive-foreground.
Do not use: On any surface other than color/brand/destructive.
Use instead: color/status/danger/foreground for text on danger status backgrounds.
Status: Stable

secondary-hover.$description:
Intent:      Light brand-tinted surface for lower-emphasis brand presence
Use when:    Secondary button fill, selected row highlight, brand-tinted badge background, active nav item background
Do not use:  High-emphasis CTAs — too light to read as a primary action
Use instead: color/brand/primary for high-emphasis filled actions
Foreground:  color/brand/secondary/foreground
Status:      active

secondary-active.$description:
Intent:      Light brand-tinted surface for lower-emphasis brand presence
Use when:    Secondary button fill, selected row highlight, brand-tinted badge background, active nav item background
Do not use:  High-emphasis CTAs — too light to read as a primary action
Use instead: color/brand/primary for high-emphasis filled actions
Foreground:  color/brand/secondary/foreground
Status:      active

destructive-hover.$description: Destructive button background on hover. Aliases color/red/700.

destructive-active.$description: Destructive button background on active/pressed. Aliases color/red/800.

default.$description:
Intent:      Background for cards and flat inline content containers
Use when:    Card backgrounds, list item backgrounds, form section backgrounds, any container sitting on top of the page canvas
Do not use:  The page canvas itself — use color/background/default for the page
             Floating or elevated UI — use color/surface/overlay for dropdowns and modals
Use instead: color/background/default for the page, color/surface/overlay for floating UI
Foreground:  color/surface/default/foreground
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon color inside a color/surface/default container
Use when:    Text and icons inside cards, list items, and flat content containers
Do not use:  Text directly on the page canvas — use color/background/default/foreground
Use instead: color/text/secondary for subdued text inside surface containers
Status:      active

raised.$description:
Intent:      Slightly elevated surface for elements that sit above the page but below overlays
Use when:    Navigation bars, sticky headers, section headers, sidebar backgrounds, inline panels that feel lifted without floating
Do not use:  Cards on a white page — the tint provides no contrast against white canvas
             Modals, dropdowns, or tooltips — use color/surface/overlay for floating UI
Use instead: color/surface/default for cards, color/surface/overlay for floating elements
Foreground:  color/surface/raised/foreground
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon color on a color/surface/raised background
Use when:    Nav labels, sidebar text, sticky header text on the raised surface
Do not use:  Text on the page canvas or inside floating overlays
Use instead: color/surface/overlay/foreground for text inside dropdowns and modals
Status:      active

overlay.$description:
Intent:      Background for floating UI elements that layer above page content
Use when:    Dropdowns, tooltips, popovers, modals, command palettes, context menus
Do not use:  Cards or flat inline content — use color/surface/default for non-floating containers
Use instead: color/surface/default for flat containers, color/surface/raised for sticky bars
Foreground:  color/surface/overlay/foreground
Note:        Resolves to the same primitive as color/surface/default today; keep the distinction so floating layers can change on their own.
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon color inside floating overlay surfaces
Use when:    Dropdown options, tooltip text, modal body text, popover content
Do not use:  Text on flat cards or the page canvas
Use instead: color/surface/default/foreground for text inside flat cards
Status:      active

muted.$description:
Intent:      Neutral, low-emphasis component fill
Use when:    Disabled input and field fills, chips, subtle neutral backgrounds inside components
Do not use:  The avatar fallback — use color/surface/tint; page-level muted sections — use color/background/muted; read-only fields — use color/input/bg-readonly
Use instead: color/surface/tint for brand-tinted identity fills
Foreground:  color/surface/muted/foreground
Note:        Shared by 7 components (input, select, textarea, combobox, slider, item, toast) — changing it changes all of them.
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Foreground on muted surface — text and icons on color/surface/muted
Note: 2026-09-22 → zinc/600 (slate) — zinc/500 was 4.34:1 on the muted fill after the slate swap.

tint.$description:
Intent:      Light brand-blue fill for identity and decorative marks
Use when:    Avatar initials fallback; other small identity fills that should feel on-brand rather than grey
Do not use:  Selected or active states — use color/sidebar/active or component tokens; info messages — use color/status/info-subtle; disabled fields — use color/surface/muted
Use instead: color/surface/muted for neutral, disabled-looking fills
Foreground:  color/surface/tint/foreground
Note:        Added 2026-09-22 for the avatar fallback; blue/100 (blue/50 read too pale).
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon on color/surface/tint
Use when:    Avatar initials
Do not use:  On any other fill
Use instead: the paired /foreground of that fill
Note:        Blue/800 — dark text from the same family as the fill; 9.51:1 on blue/100 (zinc/500 fails at 4.33).
Status:      active

success.$description:
Intent:      Filled success surface for high-emphasis positive feedback
Use when:    Success badge fill, success toast fill, confirmed state indicator
Do not use:  Success messages on a white page — use color/status/success-subtle for inline alerts
Use instead: color/status/success-subtle for low-emphasis success backgrounds
Foreground:  color/status/success/foreground
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon on a filled success surface
Use when:    Label inside a filled success badge or toast
Do not use:  Text on color/status/success-subtle — contrast fails on the light tint
Use instead: color/status/success-subtle/foreground for text on the subtle tint
Status:      active

success-subtle.$description:
Intent:      Light success tint for low-emphasis inline alerts and banners
Use when:    Success alert banner background, valid input highlight, confirmation section bg
Do not use:  Filled badges or toasts that need strong visual weight
Use instead: color/status/success for high-emphasis filled surfaces
Foreground:  color/status/success-subtle/foreground
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon on the success subtle tint
Use when:    Message text and icons inside a success alert banner
Do not use:  Text on the filled green surface — use color/status/success/foreground instead
Use instead: color/status/success/foreground for text on filled success surfaces
Status:      active

warning.$description:
Intent:      Filled warning surface for high-emphasis cautionary feedback
Use when:    Warning badge fill, caution toast fill, approaching-limit indicator
Do not use:  Error or failure states — warning signals caution, not failure
Use instead: color/status/danger for errors, color/status/warning-subtle for inline alerts
Foreground:  color/status/warning/foreground
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon on a filled warning surface
Use when:    Label inside a filled warning badge or toast
Do not use:  On any surface other than color/status/warning — dark text on light bg loses meaning
Note:        Uses zinc/900 not white — yellow/500 does not pass WCAG contrast with white text
Use instead: color/status/warning-subtle/foreground for text on the subtle tint
Status:      active

warning-subtle.$description:
Intent:      Light warning tint for low-emphasis cautionary alerts and banners
Use when:    Warning alert banner background, non-critical notice section bg
Do not use:  Error states — cautionary tint is not strong enough to signal failure
Use instead: color/status/danger-subtle for error banners, color/status/warning for filled badges
Foreground:  color/status/warning-subtle/foreground
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon on the warning subtle tint
Use when:    Message text and icons inside a warning alert banner
Do not use:  Text on the filled yellow surface — use color/status/warning/foreground instead
Use instead: color/status/warning/foreground for text on filled warning surfaces
Status:      active

danger.$description:
Intent:      Filled danger surface for high-emphasis error or destructive feedback
Use when:    Error badge fill, destructive action toast, delete confirmation indicator
Do not use:  Cautionary or non-failure states — danger signals failure, not caution
Use instead: color/status/warning for cautionary states, color/status/danger-subtle for inline alerts
Foreground:  color/status/danger/foreground
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon on a filled danger surface
Use when:    Label inside a filled error badge, icon inside a destructive toast
Do not use:  Text on color/status/danger-subtle — contrast fails on the light tint
Use instead: color/status/danger-subtle/foreground for text on the subtle tint
Status:      active

danger-subtle.$description:
Intent:      Light danger tint for low-emphasis error alerts and invalid field highlights
Use when:    Error alert banner background, invalid input field background, form error section
Do not use:  Filled badges or toasts that need strong visual weight
Use instead: color/status/danger for high-emphasis filled surfaces
Foreground:  color/status/danger-subtle/foreground
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon on the danger subtle tint
Use when:    Error message text and icons inside an alert banner or invalid input
Do not use:  Text on the filled red surface — use color/status/danger/foreground instead
Use instead: color/status/danger/foreground for text on filled danger surfaces
Status:      active

info.$description:
Intent:      Filled info surface for high-emphasis informational feedback
Use when:    Info badge fill, informational toast fill, neutral announcement indicator
Do not use:  Brand interactive elements — info is for communication, not action
Use instead: color/brand/primary for interactive CTAs, color/status/info-subtle for inline notices
Foreground:  color/status/info/foreground
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon on a filled info surface
Use when:    Label inside a filled info badge or toast
Do not use:  Text on color/status/info-subtle — contrast fails on the light tint
Use instead: color/status/info-subtle/foreground for text on the subtle tint
Status:      active

info-subtle.$description:
Intent:      Light info tint for low-emphasis informational alerts and banners
Use when:    Info alert banner background, announcement section bg, tip highlight
Do not use:  Brand interactive elements or filled badges needing strong weight
Use instead: color/status/info for high-emphasis filled surfaces
Foreground:  color/status/info-subtle/foreground
Status:      active

foreground.$description:
Intent:      Text and icon on the info subtle tint
Use when:    Message text and icons inside an informational alert banner
Do not use:  Text on the filled blue info surface — use color/status/info/foreground instead
Use instead: color/status/info/foreground for text on filled info surfaces
Status:      active

border.$description:
Intent:      Resting border color for input fields, select field, combobox field and form controls
Use when:    Text input border, textarea border, select border, checkbox outline at rest
Do not use:  Card or container borders — inputs use zinc/300, one step darker than card borders (zinc/200), to clearly define the field boundary
Use instead: color/border/focus on :focus-visible, color/border/error on invalid, color/border/disabled on disabled
Status:      active

placeholder.$description:
Intent: Text color for placeholder content inside input fields, select, combobox
Use when: The placeholder attribute text in text inputs, textareas, and select fields before a value is entered.
Do not use: For actual input value text — use color/background/default/foreground for typed content.
Use instead: color/text/disabled if the entire input is disabled, not just empty.
Status:      active

bg.$description:
Intent:      Background fill for all input-type controls (text input, textarea, combobox trigger, select trigger, date-picker trigger, OTP slot, chat input)
Use when:    Any editable field container that the user types into or selects from
Do not use:  Non-editable containers, cards, panels — use color/surface/* for those
Use instead: color/surface/muted for the disabled state of the same input
Status:      active

bg-readonly.$description:
Intent:      Input and textarea fill when read-only
Use when:    Value is shown but cannot be edited (readOnly) — still focusable and selectable
Do not use:  Disabled fields — use color/surface/muted
Note:        From En UI readonly state. Same grey as surface/muted today; kept separate so it can change on its own
Status:      active

border-readonly.$description:
Intent:      Input and textarea border when read-only — stays the normal border, no hover change
Use when:    readOnly inputs and textareas
Do not use:  Disabled fields — use color/border/disabled
Status:      active

ring.$description:
Intent:      Outer focus ring halo applied to interactive elements on keyboard focus
Use when:    box-shadow focus ring on buttons, inputs, links — the visible glow outside the element border
Do not use:  As a border replacement — ring is additive, always layered on top of the element border
Note:        shadcn core token (maps to --ring). Used alongside color/border/focus on inputs, and standalone on buttons and links that have no explicit border
Status:      active

drop-indicator.$description:
Intent:      Visual insertion line showing where dragged content will be placed
Use when:    Displaying the active drop position while reordering cards, rows or list items
Do not use:  Focus rings, selected borders, static dividers or drag handles
Use instead: color/ring for keyboard focus, color/border/default for static separation
Status:      active

default.$description:
Intent:      Default color for standalone icons on light/white surfaces
Use when:    Icons beside body text, nav icons, toolbar icons, any icon on a neutral background
Do not use:  Icons inside filled buttons, badges, or colored containers
Use instead: The container's /foreground token — e.g. color/brand/primary/foreground for an icon inside a filled blue button
Status:      active

muted.$description:
Intent:      Subdued icon for secondary or decorative use
Use when:    Supporting icons, placeholder hints, inactive nav items, decorative flourishes
Do not use:  Icons that carry meaning or need high visibility
Use instead: color/icon/default for primary icons
Status:      active

disabled.$description:
Intent:      Icon color in disabled or unavailable states
Use when:    Icons inside disabled buttons, inactive tabs, unavailable menu items
Do not use:  Any interactive or active icon state
Use instead: color/icon/default for the active equivalent
Status:      active

inverse.$description:
Intent:      Icon color on dark or inverted surfaces
Use when:    Icons on color/background/inverted, dark hero sections, dark nav bars
Do not use:  Icons on any light surface — will be invisible against white
Use instead: color/icon/default on light surfaces
Status:      active

brand.$description:
Intent:      Brand-colored icon sitting on a neutral or white surface
Use when:    Feature highlight icons, logo marks, icons that signal brand identity on light bg
Do not use:  Icons inside a filled primary button or any filled brand container — blue icon on blue fill is invisible
Use instead: color/brand/primary/foreground for icons inside filled brand containers
Status:      active

danger.$description:
Intent:      Danger or error icon on a light surface
Use when:    Error icon beside a validation message, destructive action icon on white bg
Do not use:  Icons inside a filled danger badge or filled danger button
Use instead: color/status/danger/foreground for icons inside filled danger containers
Status:      active

success.$description:
Intent:      Success or confirmation icon on a light surface
Use when:    Checkmark beside a success message, completion icon on white bg
Do not use:  Icons inside a filled success badge or toast
Use instead: color/status/success/foreground for icons inside filled success containers
Status:      active

warning.$description:
Intent:      Warning or caution icon on a light surface
Use when:    Warning icon beside a non-critical alert message on white bg
Do not use:  Icons inside a filled warning container
Use instead: color/status/warning/foreground for icons inside filled warning containers
Status:      active

background.$description:
Intent:      Fill of the Default and Inset sidebars
Use when:    Sidebar type Default / Inset
Do not use:  The Floating sidebar — it has no fill and sits directly on color/background/app

xxs.$description:
Intent:      Tightest internal spacing for compact component elements
Use when:    Icon-to-label gap inside a badge or chip, gap between a checkbox and its label, padding inside a tag or small pill
Do not use:  Padding inside buttons or cards — too tight for comfortable interaction targets
Use instead: spacing/component/sm for button padding, spacing/component/md for card padding
Status:      active

sm.$description:
Intent:      Standard tight spacing for small component internals
Use when:    Button vertical padding, input field vertical padding, icon button padding, gap between stacked labels inside a list item
Do not use:  Layout gaps between components or sections
Use instead: spacing/layout/xs for gaps between components
Status:      active

lg.$description:
Intent:      Default internal padding for most components
Use when:    Card padding, modal padding, input horizontal padding, dropdown item padding, the go-to internal spacing when unsure
Do not use:  Gaps between layout sections — use spacing/layout/* for structural spacing
Use instead: spacing/component/sm for tight components, spacing/component/lg for spacious ones
Status:      active

xl.$description:
Intent:      Generous internal padding for large or prominent components
Use when:    Large card padding, hero section inner padding, empty state padding, dialog/modal body padding
Do not use:  Small components like buttons or chips — too much breathing room
Use instead: spacing/component/md for standard components
Status:      active

2xl.$description:
Intent:      Maximum internal spacing for very large containers
Use when:    Full-page panel padding, wide modal padding, feature card inner padding
Do not use:  Regular components — reserve for large-format containers only
Use instead: spacing/component/lg for standard large components
Status:      active

xs.$description:
Intent:      Tightest internal spacing for compact component elements
Use when:    Icon-to-label gap inside a badge or chip, gap between a checkbox and its label, padding inside a tag or small pill
Do not use:  Padding inside buttons or cards — too tight for comfortable interaction targets
Use instead: spacing/component/sm for button padding, spacing/component/md for card padding
Status:      active

Intent:      Minimum gap between adjacent components in a layout
Use when:    Gap between a label and an input, gap between inline buttons, tight grid gutters in a dense UI
Do not use:  Internal component padding — use spacing/component/* for inside components
Use instead: spacing/layout/sm for standard component gaps

sm.$description:
Intent:      Standard gap between components and groups
Use when:    Gap between form fields, gap between cards in a grid, gap between nav items, space between a heading and its content block
Do not use:  Internal component padding or full section spacing
Use instead: spacing/layout/xs for tighter groups, spacing/layout/md for looser groups
Status:      active

md.$description:

Use when:    Gap between form sections, space between a page title and its content, vertical rhythm between content blocks on a page
Do not use:  Internal component padding or micro-spacing within a component
Use instead: spacing/layout/sm for tighter groups, spacing/layout/lg for major sections
Status:      active

lg.$description:
Intent:      Major section spacing for clear visual breaks between page areas
Use when:    Vertical gap between page sections, top padding of a content section, space between a hero and the next content block
Do not use:  Component-level spacing — this scale is for page structure only
Use instead: spacing/layout/md for content group gaps, spacing/layout/xl for hero-level spacing

xl.$description:

Use when:    Hero section vertical padding, top-of-page breathing room, space between major landmark sections (hero → features → pricing)

gap.$description:

Use when:    Between the sidebar, the page panel and the chat panel

inset.$description:

disabled.$description:
Intent: Reduces visual prominence of disabled UI elements to signal non-interactivity.
Use when: Any element in a disabled state — buttons, inputs, selects, checkboxes, form controls.
Do not use: For loading states — use opacity/loading instead. Do not use for placeholder content.
Use instead: opacity/loading for in-progress states, opacity/ghost for subtle but interactive elements.
Status: Stable

loading.$description:
Intent: Signals that an element is in a loading or processing state.
Use when: Skeleton loaders, buttons with loading spinners, content areas awaiting data.
Do not use: For disabled elements — use opacity/disabled instead. Loading implies the element will become active; disabled implies it cannot be used.
Use instead: opacity/disabled for permanently non-interactive elements.
Status: Stable

overlay.$description:
Intent: Semi-transparent scrim behind modal dialogs, drawers, and full-screen overlays.
Use when: The backdrop blanket behind a modal, dialog, or drawer — darkens the page to focus attention on the foreground layer.
Do not use: On the modal content itself — only on the backdrop element behind it.
Status: Stable

ghost.$description:
Intent: Slightly reduced opacity for ghost or subtle interactive elements that are still active.
Use when: Ghost buttons in their default state, secondary actions that should recede visually, watermark-style decorative elements.
Do not use: For disabled elements — ghost elements are still interactive. Use opacity/disabled for non-interactive states.
Status: Stable

active.$description:
Intent: Slightly reduced opacity for ghost or subtle interactive elements that are still active.
Use when: Ghost buttons in their default state, secondary actions that should recede visually, watermark-style decorative elements.
Do not use: For disabled elements — ghost elements are still interactive. Use opacity/disabled for non-interactive states.
Status: Stable

control.$description: Role radius (from En UI radius-control). Use for: Buttons, inputs, selects, comboboxes, date pickers.

surface.$description: Role radius (from En UI radius-surface). Use for: Cards, panels, tables, form groups.

overlay.$description: Role radius (from En UI radius-overlay). Use for: Popovers, menus, dialogs, sheets.

pill.$description: Role radius (from En UI radius-pill). Use for: Badges, avatars, pills.

panel.$description:
Intent:      Corner radius of floating app-shell panels — 12px
Use when:    The floating sidebar, the page panel, the chat panel
Do not use:  Cards, controls, popovers — use radius/surface, radius/control, radius/overlay
Use instead: radius/surface for cards

hairline.$description: Role shadow (from En UI shadow-hairline). Use for: Inner edge of layered surfaces.

surface.$description: Role shadow (from En UI shadow-surface). Use for: Default containers — cards, panels, tables. Pairs with border/default.

raised.$description: Role shadow (from En UI shadow-raised). Use for: Sticky regions; a card only while dragged or pinned above scrolling content.

overlay.$description: Role shadow (from En UI shadow-overlay). Use for: Popovers, menus, tooltips, dialogs and alert dialogs.

modal.$description: Role shadow (from En UI shadow-modal). Use for: Dialogs and sheets.

xs.$description:
Intent:      Control height, xs — 24px from the sm breakpoint (640px) up, where a mouse or trackpad is the pointer
Use when:    Dense table rows, toolbars, inline row actions. Always paired with the touch rung: h-[var(--height-control-touch-xs)] sm:h-[var(--height-control-xs)]
Do not use:  Alone without the touch class — phones would get the smaller mouse size
Use instead: height/control-touch/xs (28px) below 640px
Note:        From En UI --height-control-xs. drift-check fails on hardcoded control heights.
Status:      active

sm.$description:
Intent:      Control height, sm — 28px from the sm breakpoint (640px) up, where a mouse or trackpad is the pointer
Use when:    Compact controls in filters, secondary forms. Always paired with the touch rung: h-[var(--height-control-touch-sm)] sm:h-[var(--height-control-sm)]
Do not use:  Alone without the touch class — phones would get the smaller mouse size
Use instead: height/control-touch/sm (32px) below 640px
Note:        From En UI --height-control-sm. drift-check fails on hardcoded control heights.
Status:      active

md.$description:
Intent:      Control height, md — 32px from the sm breakpoint (640px) up, where a mouse or trackpad is the pointer
Use when:    The default for buttons, inputs, selects, comboboxes, date pickers, menu option rows. Always paired with the touch rung: h-[var(--height-control-touch-md)] sm:h-[var(--height-control-md)]

min.$description:

Note:        From En UI --height-target-touch. Advisory for primary and touch-heavy actions.
